title: Event-time bars from saved sessions: coverage and feature distributions
verdictNote: The bars are built correctly as far as we can check: flow imbalance moves with the same bar's return (rho 0.638), no bar spans a session or a long silence, and the spread, trade counts and sizes match what the market looks like. But the second check fixed in advance FAILED: we expected the next bar's return to be nearly unrelated to this bar's flow and return, and it is not (rho 0.257 and 0.171). Consecutive bars tile one continuous trade stream, so a burst of orders can be cut into several bars; the dependence may be that slicing rather than anything tradable, and the pairs overlap in time so no p-value is claimed. The lag table below shows how far it reaches. Followed up in the entry dependence-slicing-vs-persistence-2026-10-29: it is mostly the slicing of bursts into bars. Near-touch depth is the top 10 levels (Binance snapshots hold only about 0.5 bps of the book); wider depth lives in the collector data and comes later.
question: Can our saved sessions be turned into event-time bars with a sensible feature vector, and what do the bars look like (size, duration, flow, price, depth, time of day)?

method.summary: Dollar bars on Binance trades: a bar closes when its trades add up to the bar size, so activity sets the clock. Bar size chosen from the data so a bar lasts about 10 s on average (the median is 3.721 s: activity comes in bursts, so most bars are short and a few are long; 6.7% close within the same millisecond) (1,300,000 USD). Per bar: aggressor flow and imbalance, OHLC, return in bps and in sigmas (ADR 0004 scale, from the previous 30 minutes only), near-touch depth and its imbalance and change, spread, Hyperliquid flow in the same window, Binance sweeps, largest-trade share, hour of day. Bars never span sessions or a silence over 60 s.
plan: Bar size is decided from the data before looking at any relationship, and is not tuned afterwards.

Sanity checks fixed in advance: flow imbalance should correlate positively with the same bar's return; the next bar's return should be nearly unrelated to this bar's flow (did not hold, see the verdict).
Rank (Spearman) correlation, descriptive only; no test is claimed in this entry.

results.text: Bars are descriptive. A correlation here is a check that the bars are built correctly, not a market finding.
